scores.visual_critic_note: Deliberate TOL palette with rank-encoded colors, clean typographic hierarchy, and polished search/count affordances — but the bottom half of the viewport is wasted empty space with the tree occupying only the top 50%.
scores.encoding_integrity_note: Tree topology visualization with no quantitative visual channels — categorical color encoding is honest, layout dimensions are fully data-driven via d3.extent/d3.max, and no baseline, lie-factor, or dual-axis violations apply; minor: node key uses name+depth concatenation which could theoretically collide but is fine for this dataset.
scores.stress_test_note: No .interrupt() calls before new transitions, and the g-group uses a separate 400ms transition while nodes use a 500ms transition via svgEl, causing mild visual desync on rapid clicks; search is properly debounced, pointer events avoid mouse-touch fights, and no stale scale closures or cross-view feedback loops exist.
scores.cognitive_load_note: Progressive disclosure keeps the default view to ~15 nodes across 2 levels, the 6-color Tol palette maps cleanly to ranks, and +N count badges communicate hidden complexity without exposing it — cognitive load stays low until the user deliberately expands deep; animation quality and fully-expanded scroll length (200 nodes at 22px each) can't be fully assessed from the static screenshot.

proposer: 538 → 529 lines (-9). Inlined `showTooltip`, `moveTooltip`, and `setAllExpanded` — each was used only once.
